newsitem.title: THAILAND: Foreigners fleeing Cambodia arrive in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners fleeing Cambodia arrive in Bangkok.

text.p: Three Thai Airforce C-130 planes arrived in Bangkok from Cambodia on Tuesday, carrying some 300 Thais and other foreigners who fled fighting in Phnom Penh.
Thailand's Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn and other senior officials were on the tarmac to meet those who returned, mostly women and children.
The planes had flown to Phnom Penh's battered airport earlier on Tuesday.
Those who alighted from the first plane were seen wearing yellow ribbons on their wrists as identification tags.
They were among several hundred people who had waited at Phnom Penh's airport on Tuesday to escape the Cambodian capital after three days of fighting and turmoil.
Among those who stepped off the rescue plane was American Gary Jahn from Phoenix, Arizona, who arrived with his two children and Thai wife.

"We had no problems coming back, it was fairly quiet (in Phnom Penh) and we formed a convoy and went to the airport," said Jahn who works for the International Rice Research Institute on a project in Cambodia.

"The Cambodian People's Party (of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen) has secured the city, but there is a lot of damage. We saw a lot of damage and passed a blown up tank on the way to the airport," he told Reuters.
Jahn said shells fell close to where he lived during fighting between Hun Sen's forces and those of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

He followed events through the Internet and through calls from the United States. Jahn managed to leave with his family because of his Thai wife but vowed to return to continue working on his project in Cambodia as soon as possible.

A Swiss man, who identified himself as Andre, escaped from Phnom Penh with his wife and teenaged daughter. They had arrived in Cambodia for a holiday on Saturday but found they could not leave after fighting broke out over the weekend.

"On the way to the airport we saw a lot of damage. Car showrooms had been looted and there was a lot of destroyed property and damaged vehicles," he said. "The airport runway and facilities at the airport were damaged."
Immigration officials at Bangkok airport set up special tables to swiftly clear the evacuees who were also served refreshments.
Foreign minister Prachuab said a total of seven planes would be sent to evacuate foreigners from Phnom Penh, especially 707 Thais who would be given first priority.
He expected the arrival of the four other planes to be somewhat delayed as there were many other people to be picked up at the airport in Phnom Penh.
On the situation in Cambodia, Prachuab said the situation was unsettled although fighting had ebbed.
"As far as we have heard, the fighting is over but of course the situation is unsettled. There may be some scattered shooting," he said.

Prachuab said embassies of other foreign countries had contacted Thai authorities to seek assistance in evacuating their citizens. "We are coordinating with them and we may bring out some of their people," he added without elaborating.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said separately that he did not believe the Cambodian crisis would harm relations between the two countries.
"I don't think the crisis in Cambodia would mean the end of relations between the two countries," he told reporters.
